primitives.name: Orinq receipts pallet
primitives.desc: Receipt registry with M-of-N committee attestation, availability certification, anchor records, attestor bonds and slashing, and fee escrow — the on-chain truth every other primitive commits to.

primitives.name: MOTRA fee resource
primitives.desc: Non-transferable transaction-fee resource generated from MATRA holdings (NIGHT/DUST model), charged by a signed extension, with sponsor delegation; the extension also gives a runtime-named (signer, call) set the top transaction-pool priority, one slot per signer, so the guardian's veto cannot be outbid for a place in a block.

primitives.name: Billing pallet
primitives.desc: Application-layer MATRA billing (pay_request) for API calls, metering and attestation evidence — the user-facing spend surface, distinct from MOTRA tx fees.

primitives.name: TEE attestation pallet
primitives.desc: Hardware attestation-evidence registry (secp256r1 and ARM TrustZone phone attestors) binding TEE quotes to receipts.

primitives.name: Committee seating gate
primitives.desc: Composed authority-selection gate: input sanitizer, dead-registered and dead-core liveness filters, seat-ramp clamp, live-quorum floor, growth-slack invariant, break-glass floor and pinned-committee override; refuses (keep-current) rather than seat a committee that cannot finalize.

primitives.name: Main-chain follower
primitives.desc: Cardano main-chain follower backends (db-sync and yaci-store with Mithril-certified stake) supplying candidate registrations and the D-parameter to authority selection.

primitives.name: Mainnet launch preflight
primitives.desc: Fail-closed genesis and launch gate: reads the raw chain spec, the runtime metadata extracted from its code, the authority launch commands (opening sh -c wrappers) and each authority's running node argv from a /proc/<pid>/cmdline capture, the nginx and cloudflared RPC proxy configs, each public RPC URL probed live over HTTP and a WebSocket, and Cardano mainnet through Kupo (the cMATRA genesis lock and its datum, and the permissioned candidates datum). Refuses on a well-known key anywhere (genesis, runtime code, any role or multisig member, the Cardano committee, node configs including dev-phrase URIs and the dev seed, the signing key), Sudo.Key or a genesis account no declared role accounts for, Root not a multisig two keyholders must sign for (one key that meets its threshold alone through a nested multisig counts as one keyholder) or one with a multisig at any depth of more members than the runtime's Multisig.MaxSignatories, which pallet_multisig never signs through, an undeclared off-chain role, a chain spec the anchor worker would read as a test network, attestor or validator reward parameters that are undeclared or not what genesis and the runtime hold, unsafe RPC on an authority, a public RPC URL that lists a method outside the safe set or answers an unsafe one, an authority with no launch entry, under-endowed attestors, genesis storage outside an allowlist, issuance plus the runtime's emission reserves above what the genesis lock holds, a lock fewer than two key holders can spend or not bound to this genesis, PerpEngine under any name, a runtime override or code substitute, a genesis-enabled Cardano deposit observation with no checkpoint, genesis, code, chain-spec and launch manifest hashes that differ from a manifest signed by a launch key the repo pins, a Root timelock guardian missing from genesis, not the declared multisig, not needing two keyholders or over MaxSignatories by the same test as Root, with a nested multisig member (whose veto the runtime does not take first), the sudo key or sharing any account or member with it, or timelock delays missing, below the runtime's mainnet delays, above its MaxDelay or out of order, both read from the runtime metadata; and hex in the raw spec, the manifests, the launch keys or the key tables in any spelling but the one its writer writes, or a JSON object in them that names a key twice, since the node reads another spelling as other bytes.

primitives.name: Root timelock
primitives.desc: Holds every non-exempt Root call for a per-class delay (recovery for committee toggles and delay raises, the standard delay for everything else including consensus-key levers, sudo key rotation and kill-switch restarts unless the guardian co-signs, long for the dedicated bridge and supply levers) in a bounded vetoable queue with a guardian veto, bulk veto, fast-track and a one-shot advance approval that Root runs without a queue place, plus one guardian change the guardian cannot veto and the sudo key can withdraw; the runtime call filter lets the sudo key reach Root at once only for pause, withdrawal and session-bounded finality break-glass calls, for scheduling and for the approved call, each timelock call is charged for every call its classifier walks, and genesis refuses a chain spec without an independent guardian, or with a development account as guardian, and allows an unguarded one only when its sudo key is a development account or absent. Its mainnet delays (DefaultDelays) and their ceiling (MaxDelay) are metadata constants, so a genesis audit can bound the stored delays from the runtime alone. The guardian's veto and co-sign calls (cancel, cancel_all, fast_track, approve), signed by the current guardian directly or through a multisig as_multi wrapper, are given the top transaction-pool priority through the MOTRA fee extension, bounded to one slot per signer and to the wrapped call's own weight, so a stolen sudo key cannot buy its way past the veto and a compromised guardian cannot use the priority to fill blocks.
